To address the safety concerns and collisions at this intersection, the administration recommends channelization on Main Street.
Channelization involves modifying the existing mediums on both Main Street approaches to create right turn only lanes.
Drivers on Main Street will be required to turn right at the intersection, and will no longer be able to drive straight through or turn left onto Clarence Avenue.

This will eliminate the potential for right angle collisions, address the existing sightline issues for the left turn and through movements, and with a side benefit of reducing short cutting traffic on Main Street.
Next slide, please.

Three alternatives were considered but not recommended. The first was improving the sightlines by removing 14 mature Elm trees. This would help, but the potential for right angle collisions would still exist.
The second was an always stop. The assessment showed that this does not meet the criteria for an always stop.
Primarily due to the large traffic volume on Clarence Avenue, and it also have a negative byproduct by of increasing short cutting on Main Street.

Finally, traffic signals were assessed. This would require nine trees to be removed, would cause delays to Clarence Avenue traffic, and would also have a negative byproduct of increasing short cutting traffic on Main Street.
